headline: Profit and margins surge as revenue dips modestly
summary_short: Gentex's Q2 2026 revenue slipped 1.0% y/y to $651.3M, but gross margin expanded 280bps to 37.0% and diluted EPS rose 25.6% y/y to a Q2 record $0.54, aided by roughly $18M of IEEPA tariff reimbursements.
summary_long: Net sales fell 1.0% y/y to $651.3M as a ~3% q/q automotive decline (Europe, Japan/Korea, China) was mostly offset by North America strength and 16% Premium Audio growth. Gross margin rose 280bps y/y to 37.0% on ~$18M of IEEPA tariff reimbursements and favorable mix, lifting operating income 19.3% to $141.3M despite lower revenue. Net income rose 19.4% to $114.7M; diluted EPS was $0.54 (+25.6% y/y), a Q2 record. The company repurchased $66.0M of stock in the quarter; cash rose to $233.4M q/q. FY2026 guidance: revenue unchanged at $2.65-2.75B, gross margin raised to 34.5-35.5%, capex and opex ranges lowered, tax-rate range narrowed lower.

drivers.explanation: Automotive revenue fell ~3% q/q on weakness in Europe, Japan/Korea, and China, mostly offset by North American strength, a 16% q/q rise in Premium Audio, and ~12% q/q growth in Other Products.
Cost of goods sold fell mainly on ~$18M of IEEPA tariff reimbursements and favorable product mix, partially offset by commodity cost increases and lower sales volume.
Gross margin expanded 280bps y/y to 37.0% on ~$18M of IEEPA tariff reimbursements and favorable product mix, partly offset by commodity cost increases and the sales decline.
Higher gross margin plus lower operating expenses (prior-year severance costs did not repeat) drove the 19.3% increase despite lower revenue.
Tracked the operating income increase, partly offset by a wider other-loss from credit-loss reserves and a technology-investment impairment charge.
Higher pretax income and a lower effective tax rate (16.5% vs 17.2% a year earlier) drove the 19.4% increase.
Higher net income combined with a reduced diluted share count from ongoing buybacks lifted diluted EPS to a Q2 record.
Same drivers as diluted EPS: higher net income and a reduced basic share count from ongoing buybacks.
Growth in retained earnings from net income was partially offset by $66.0M of share repurchases during the quarter.
Share count fell y/y as the company continued repurchasing stock: 2.7M shares ($66.0M) this quarter, 5.9M shares ($137.6M) year-to-date.

Tariff reimbursements and favorable mix drove record Q2 margins and EPS despite a modest revenue decline from automotive/China softness, prompting raised FY2026 margin guidance and lowered capex/opex guidance.
